entries.reason: a continuation of the DeviceCheck surface registry/DeviceCheck/ios11.json carried, which names as not carried "DCAppAttestService and the attestation keys, came in iOS 14"
entries.effect: the class exists beside DCDevice in the Foundation library; +sharedService is one shared object, -isSupported is NO, and the three calls answer the documented error from a background queue after the call returns
entries.source: the host's own DeviceCheck under MacOSX.sdk, which is a platform with no App Attest service: -isSupported answers NO, +sharedService is one object, -generateKeyWithCompletionHandler: answers DCErrorFeatureUnsupported (1) and -attestKey:clientDataHash:completionHandler: and -generateAssertion:clientDataHash:completionHandler: answer DCErrorInvalidInput (2), each after the call and off the main thread

entries.reason: the service of the framework is a single object, as it is where the service runs
entries.effect: one DCAppAttestService, made once and the same object every time, as the host's own answers
entries.source: the host's own DeviceCheck under MacOSX.sdk, asked twice

entries.reason: App Attest is the Secure Enclave's service and these devices have no Secure Enclave - it came with the A7 of the iPhone 5s - so the question has the answer the framework gives a device without it
entries.effect: -isSupported is NO; the header documents NO for a device type that does not provide the service
entries.source: the host's own DeviceCheck under MacOSX.sdk, whose -[DCAppAttestService isSupported] answers NO

entries.reason: the key is made in the Secure Enclave, which these devices do not have, and no daemon of the release runs the service
entries.effect: the handler is called with a nil key id and an error in DCErrorDomain with code DCErrorFeatureUnsupported (1), which the header defines as DeviceCheck being unavailable on this device; off the main thread and after the call returns, as the host answers and as this package's DCDevice token path does; a nil handler is ignored
entries.source: the host's own DeviceCheck under MacOSX.sdk: nil key id, com.apple.devicecheck.error, code 1, on a thread that is not the main one, after the call returned

entries.reason: no key of this device was ever made, so no key a caller can name is a key that can be attested
entries.effect: the handler is called with a nil attestation object and an error in DCErrorDomain with code DCErrorInvalidInput (2), off the main thread and after the call returns; a nil handler is ignored
entries.source: the host's own DeviceCheck under MacOSX.sdk, which answers code 2 both for a nil key id and for a well-formed one with a 32 byte hash

entries.reason: an assertion is signed by an attested key, and there is none on this device
entries.effect: the handler is called with a nil assertion object and an error in DCErrorDomain with code DCErrorInvalidInput (2), off the main thread and after the call returns; a nil handler is ignored
entries.source: the host's own DeviceCheck under MacOSX.sdk, which answers code 2
